gap: No result ChatGPT got compares the host-port and SSD-power limits of the 10Gbps picks: on its own US store, UGREEN says the CM691 works with a USB-A computer only through a USB-A-to-C cable you buy separately (0.8 m or shorter) and then gives devices 5 V/2 A instead of 2.4 A, while ATEN's US3342 manual says its total output is 10 W shared by all downstream ports.
standout_why: ChatGPT cited us.ugreen.com (both URLs). That page has the CM691 USB-A note, but ChatGPT's answers ignored it and asked the shopper 'USB-C or USB-A?' instead, so having the page did not answer the question. The ATEN cap and the side-by-side comparison appear nowhere in the results. Digitaldesksolutions.com (2026-10-28) is worse than silent: under the UGREEN 10Gbps USB-C switch it lists 'No USB-A input stated' and 'Power source not listed' as cons, and the article says nobody on its team tested the units. The ATEN US3342 page ChatGPT got (neutronusa.com) is only a reseller listing, which I did not open. Pickslab, techwisereviews, macedynamics, bobmacs and howtovr were not opened (budget), so I can't rule out that one of them mentions part of this.
decides: This confirms the UGREEN CM691 as the pick and answers ChatGPT's own follow-up question. With two USB-C computers it is the simplest fit: cables in the box and 2.4 A for devices. With a USB-A computer it still works, but you need your own short USB-A-to-C cable and power drops to 5 V/2 A. That is the same 2 A ceiling as the ATEN US3342's 10 W shared budget, so the $157 ATEN gives an SSD no extra power on its downstream ports. ATEN's pass-through adapter charges the laptop and doesn't raise that 10 W. If the SSD is a power-hungry NVMe drive, look at a switch with its own power input: Cable Matters 201160 (optional 5 V 3 A input, not verified this run) or UGREEN's 7-port powered model. Separately, Mac owners on macOS 13.3 or later must set 'Allow accessories to connect' to 'Always', or devices won't work after switching.
candidates: UGREEN USB-C Switch CM691 (10Gbps, 2 in / 4 out)

findings.label: USB-A computer support
findings.value: Works with a USB-A computer through a USB-A-to-C data cable (not in the box; UGREEN says best within 0.8 m / 2.6 ft)
findings.source_title: UGREEN USBC Switch - 2-Port, 4 x USB 3.2, 10Gbps Data
findings.note: Store text: 'About USB A Laptop Only need to use a USB-A to C data cable (best within 1.2ft/0.8m)' (the feet figure is UGREEN's typo; 0.8 m is 2.6 ft, the same as the included cables). The box has 2 USB-C to C cables (0.8 m) and a 1.5 m remote. Read with storecheck.py.

findings.label: Power available to shared devices
findings.value: Up to 2.4 A when connected to a USB-C laptop port; 5 V 2 A when connected to a USB-A port
findings.source_title: UGREEN USBC Switch - 2-Port, 4 x USB 3.2, 10Gbps Data
findings.note: Bus-powered from the computer; no separate power input. UGREEN says 2.4 A is 'enough power to run four 3.5" HDD/SSD or two 2.5" 1TB HDD/SSD at once' (maker's claim, not tested). The manual spec lists 'Power Supply Input USB-C 5.0V 2.4A Max' (manualslib.com/manual/3466404/Ugreen-Cm691.html, read 2026-11-08).

findings.label: Exclusions
findings.value: Data only: no video or monitor over the USB-C inputs, and the output ports don't charge laptops or USB devices. UGREEN advises against 2.4 GHz wireless dongles because of interference. Cables longer than 0.8 m may lower speed.
findings.source_title: UGREEN USBC Switch - 2-Port, 4 x USB 3.2, 10Gbps Data
findings.note: Store text: 'This is a USB C switch not a KVM switch and doesn't support a monitor'; 'does not support power supply for a laptop/USB devices or video transmission'. The charging exclusion means the ports don't charge devices; they still bus-power them (see the 2.4 A finding).

findings.label: macOS setting and priority
findings.value: macOS 13.3 and later: set System Settings > Privacy & Security > 'Allow accessories to connect' to 'Always'. When both computers are connected, PC 1 gets priority.
findings.source_title: UGREEN USBC Switch - 2-Port, 4 x USB 3.2, 10Gbps Data
findings.note: The manual lists Windows/macOS/Linux as compatible systems.

findings.label: Price, UGREEN US store
findings.source_title: UGREEN USBC Switch - 2-Port, 4 x USB 3.2, 10Gbps Data

findings.label: Ports
findings.value: Computers: 2× USB 3.2 Gen 2 USB-C. Devices: 3× USB-A + 1× USB-C (all USB 3.2 Gen 2, 10Gbps). Separate USB-C PD 3.0 power input.
findings.source_title: US3342 2-Port USB-C Gen 2 Sharing Switch with Power Pass-through - ATEN
findings.note: This corrects our page's ATEN row, which says '4 (listings say USB-A)'. In the box: 2× USB-C 3.2 Gen 2 cables (1 m) and a remote port selector.

findings.label: Downstream power budget
findings.value: 10 W total, shared by all USB downstream ports (2 A at 5 V)
findings.source_title: ATEN US3342 User Manual, Components (manual p.11 of 29)
findings.note: Manual: 'Total output power is 10W shared by all USB downstream ports.' 10 W / 5 V = 2 A, below the CM691's 2.4 A from a USB-C host.

findings.label: Exclusions and pass-through
findings.value: USB-C monitors not supported on the computer ports. Laptop charging pass-through up to 85 W needs a separate USB-C PD adapter (ATEN recommends a single-port LPS adapter above 65 W). Basic USB power minimum is 5 V 3 A.
findings.source_title: US3342 2-Port USB-C Gen 2 Sharing Switch with Power Pass-through - ATEN
findings.note: Also on the page: BEZEL X software for Windows 10 / macOS 10.12, and touchpads aren't supported for cross-platform mouse control on macOS 14 and later.

findings.label: Latest firmware
findings.source_title: US3342 2-Port USB-C Gen 2 Sharing Switch with Power Pass-through - ATEN
findings.note: Taken from the maker page's download section.
